extracted.intended_audience: publishers, literary agents, and authors submitting works of fiction to the PEN/Faulkner Award
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility rules for submitting books of fiction (short story collections, novellas, or novels) for consideration for the annual PEN/Faulkner Award for Fiction. Covers who may submit, what works are eligible, submission mechanics, fees, and selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible authors (citizenship/residency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must be living U.S. citizens or permanent residents. U.S. citizens living abroad are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Award honors the best published works of fiction by American permanent residents in a calendar year; only living U.S. citizens or permanent residents may be submitted. (No other residency/citizenship exceptions noted.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible work types
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers, literary agents, and authors may submit works of fiction (short story collections, novellas, or novels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are explicitly limited to fiction formats listed; anthologies are later stated as not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date window
rubrics_metrics.description: Books published between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2025 are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must fall within the calendar-year publication window specified for the Award cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission period / deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission period opens July 1, 2025 and closes September 30, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We encourage submission as early as possible because the judges’ reading process begins upon receipt. Fee waiver requests must be emailed no later than 12 PM Eastern Time on Friday, September 26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher eligibility (press type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Books must be published by commercial, university, or independent presses in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that are self-published, or published by presses that charge for production or editorial services, are not eligible. This implies the press should be a legitimate U.S. publisher that does not require authors to pay for production/editorial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-published / pay-to-publish exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Books that are self-published, or published by presses that charge for production or editorial services, are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such books will be considered ineligible even if submitted; note that ineligible books remain subject to the entry fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A translation from another language into English by the author is eligible; a translation by someone other than the author is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only author-translated works into English qualify; third-party translations are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion: board members' books
rubrics_metrics.description: Books published by current PEN/Faulkner board members are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion prevents conflicts of interest between the Foundation's board and submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion: reprints and anthologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reprints are not eligible. Anthologies are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only first/publication-eligible single-author books or eligible translations (by author) in the stated publication year are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission requires a $95 entry fee and must be submitted via our online submission platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions are charged the fee; any books determined to be ineligible will still be subject to the $95 fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waiver policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the fee presents a significant financial hardship to an author submitting their own book, they may request a fee waiver by emailing Sarah Silberman (sarah@penfaulkner.org). Authors requesting a fee waiver are limited to one submission per submission period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee waiver requests must be emailed no later than 12 PM Eastern Time on Friday, September 26. Publishers and literary agents are not eligible for a fee waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method / format
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept virtual submissions via our online submission platform only. We no longer accept email submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit an easy-to-read PDF of the finished manuscript or Advanced Reading Copy (no watermarks over the body of the text) of the title. Follow the online platform's upload requirements; email submissions are explicitly rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an easy-to-read PDF of the finished manuscript or Advanced Reading Copy (no watermarks over the body of the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the PDF is readable and has no watermarks covering the body text. This refers to the file the judges will read; follow common ARC/manuscript formatting for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging panel and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Three writers are chosen annually by the Board of Directors of the PEN/Faulkner Foundation to serve as judges, ensuring that our awards selection process is free of commercial influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges are peer writers selected by the board (not commercial interests), emphasizing literary peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection stages and numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: These judges select an initial longlist of ten books, followed by five finalists, and finally one winner as the 'first among equals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is sequential: longlist (10) → finalists (5) → winner (1). Understanding this helps submitters set expectations for the competition's narrowing stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes and finalist awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The author of the winning book receives a $15,000 prize. The authors of each of the other finalists receive $5,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary awards are specified for winner and finalists; finalists are recognized and remunerated even if they do not win.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for eligibility questions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have questions about eligibility, and want to ensure you’re not charged for an ineligible entry, please contact Sarah Silberman (sarah@penfaulkner.org).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting the staff before submission can avoid wasted fees for ineligible entries; use this contact for waiver inquiries and eligibility clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to submit early / judges read upon receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage you to submit titles as early as possible. The judges’ reading process begins upon receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early submission may influence reading timelines; do not wait until the deadline since judges begin reading immediately and there is no stated 'late-batching' process.
